target_customer: Dropshippers and small resellers in Colombia, mostly women selling to neighbors and coworkers
problem: Small resellers lack suppliers, shipping, payments, credit and sales know-how to run a dropshipping business.
business_model: Marketplace and commerce operating system for dropshippers with commissions of 20 to 40 percent, shipping, payments and ad credit
product_category: Latin American dropshipping and social commerce platform

founders.name: Juan Camilo Vallejo
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he is a product manager and entrepreneur who raised about 1 million dollars previously; no employers named.

founders.name: Juan Manuel Botero
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and in Forbes Colombia Nov 2020.

founders.name: Jose Tamura
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and in Forbes Colombia Nov 2020.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with supplier catalog, order routing, shipping and payments integration is standard web engineering, with operational complexity in logistics.

defensibility.rationale: A supplier base of 160 plus and 1,000 plus sellers gave early two sided density, but dropshipping platforms such as Dropi and Mastershop later served the same market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated incumbent response found. Dropi and Mastershop appear in 2026 comparisons, with no source dating them to the batch.

market_need_then: Forbes Colombia Nov 2020 reports more than 1,000 sellers and 52 percent monthly growth, plus Colombian press (Portafolio) describing dropshipping growth during 2020.

branding.domain_note: valienta.com is the exact name domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Empowerment focused, aimed at women resellers (Portafolio headline on female inclusion)

branding.community_and_virality: Forbes Colombia named it one of the top 100 startups in Colombia in 2020, with a base of mostly women sellers.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press (Forbes Colombia, Portafolio) covered it in 2020, but no community, merch or brand story was found. The name resembles valiente, the Spanish for brave, but no source states the origin.

outcome_analysis: Valienta joined YC Winter 2020 from Medellin, reported over 1,000 sellers and about 52 percent monthly growth by November 2020, and is now marked inactive by YC with no later funding found. No shutdown notice or post-mortem was found and the valienta.com site returned 404, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: Seed rests on a single database (CB Insights 150K, 2020-03-17, YC); Forbes Colombia confirms YC as first investor without an amount. The Forbes article lists the three founders; CB Insights and Crunchbase list Botero as COO and Tamura as CTO, unopened. The valienta.com fetch returned 404. Competitor search returned 2026 sources only (Dropi, Mastershop, Effi), so the list is empty. YC page lists a dropshipping pitch while Forbes describes catalog direct selling, suggesting the model evolved during 2020.
